assumptions: Field labels (holder offsets, buffer size rule, inner size) describe observed pointer arithmetic only, not confirmed source-level types.
Sized-delete sizes are the second argument observed at each PLT call site.
The buffer-size reading ([inner+0x10] minus buffer begin) is the observed subtraction, not a claim about a source-level capacity end.
The buffer and inner ranges are treated as well-formed; a corrupt range is not modelled.
behavior: Buffer-inner teardown: load inner = [holder]; a null inner returns plainly with nothing freed. Otherwise load buffer = [inner]; a null buffer skips the buffer free, else free the buffer with a sized delete of ([inner+0x10] - buffer) bytes through the _ZdlPvm PLT at 0x63f0d80. Then tail-jump to the same PLT freeing the inner object at a fixed size of 0x18 bytes. The holder itself is never freed, and no canary check is performed.

buffer_phase.null_buffer_test: skip the buffer free, inner free still runs

consumers.note: Reached only by code, never by data. See callers.tsv for the site list.

exits.condition: inner non-null, buffer freed or skipped
exits.target: sized-delete PLT 0x63f0d80 freeing the inner object at a fixed 0x18 bytes
